finding_headline: R fable ARIMA MinT shrink is the most accurate model at 8 of 9 levels; SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,0)[52] wins Total
finding_detail: Where it wins, its WAPE runs from 3.2% to 6.3%, against 14.0% to 16.2% for seasonal naive at the same levels (6 test origins).

finding_headline: A plain 4-week moving average beats ETS at 9 of 9 levels
finding_detail: The gap is widest at Department: the moving average has WAPE 6.5% against 7.5% for ETS, so the more complex model adds nothing here.

finding_headline: LightGBM's 80% band held the actual in 12 of 24 Total forecasts (50.0%), below the 80% target
finding_detail: The average 80% band is 7.3% of weekly revenue wide. The explorer shows horizons 1 and 4 for 14 nodes; the count here uses all 4 horizons of the 6 test origins.

finding_headline: Only MinT shrink improves ARIMA at all 9 levels; bottom-up is worse by 22.7% at Total (it beats the base at 2 of 9 levels)
finding_detail: MinT shrink cuts ARIMA WAPE by 5.3% to 23.3% depending on level. For ETS it helps at 7 of 9 levels and is 6.9% worse at Total.

finding_headline: 156 of 180 model and level cases under-cover the 80% interval by more than 5 points
finding_detail: At Total the closest model is ETS (statsforecast AutoETS) at 83.3%, from only 24 forecasts. The fable bottom-up, OLS and WLS intervals cover only 12.5% to 29.2% of actuals at Total.

finding_headline: Plan store and department volumes from MinT-reconciled ARIMA: WAPE 4.0% by store, 6.3% by store and department
finding_detail: It has the lowest WAPE at 8 of 9 levels. At Total the best model, SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,0)[52], is ahead by 0.1 points, too small to matter given 6 test origins.

finding_headline: Keep the 4-week moving average as the benchmark to beat, and do not use seasonal naive (WAPE 14.0% to 16.2%)
finding_detail: The moving average's WAPE is 5.0% to 8.1% across levels and beats ETS at 9 of 9 levels. Any new model should be tested against it first.

finding_headline: ASSUMED costs: planning at the 90th percentile adds a buffer of 3.1% of revenue at Total and 8.0% at Store x Department, and cuts the ASSUMED cost by 66% at Total
finding_detail: ASSUMED parameters: 25% margin lost on unmet revenue, 5% carrying cost on excess, plan at q90. These are scenario inputs, not estimates from the data. Figures are for MinT-reconciled ARIMA.

finding_headline: Treat the buffer as a floor: only 75% of Total weeks fell within the 90th percentile plan, and intervals under-cover
finding_detail: Results come from 6 test origins (24 weeks) and 10 stores in 3 states, so re-test on your own data before committing inventory.
